title: Double `%`: `x - y·floor(x / y)`
verdict: floor remainder; NaN for `x % 0` and for finite `x % ±inf`
description: `%` on doubles computes `x - y * floor(x / y)`: the remainder has the divisor's sign (`5.5 % -2` is -0.5), `x % 0` is NaN, and a finite `x % ±inf` is NaN too (`x / inf` is 0, and `inf * 0` is NaN), where C's `fmod` and Python's `%` give `x`. The formula also loses the exactness of `fmod` for large quotients.

A zero remainder is always 0.0: `x - y * q` with equal terms is +0.0 under round to nearest, and for `x = -0.0` the product `y * q` is -0.0, so `-0.0 % y` is 0.0 too (`fmod` gives -0.0 for `-4 % 2` and `-0.0 % y`).
reference: `modulus` on doubles (sverify's `sverify_fmod`): the truncated remainder (`fmod`), with a zero divisor an error as on integers, and `fmod(x, ±inf) = x`. 60 of the 144 rows differ.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: A literal divisor: `x - rhs * (x * (1 / rhs)).floor()`; a literal dividend: `lhs - x * (lhs / x).floor()`.
`+ - * // %` on two ChunkedArrays: equal lengths take the array kernel, a length-1 side the scalar kernel.
A literal is a scalar column, passed to the operation as a one-value Series.
The streaming engine evaluates each expression with polars-expr's `PhysicalExpr` on every morsel, so it runs the same kernels.

notes: `impl_float_arith_kernel!` is one macro instantiated for `pf16`, `f32` and `f64`, so `Float32` and `Float64` run the same operations. The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (`StreamExpr` in crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so it shares these kernels with the in-memory engine. So the floor remainder, NaN for a zero divisor and NaN for a finite `x % ±inf` hold for `Float32` as the `Float64` probes show.

With a literal divisor on a frame of two rows or more, the kernel multiplies by the reciprocal: where `x * (1 / y)` rounds below an integer that `x / y` reaches, the floor is one less and the remainder is `y` itself (`49.0 % 49.0` is 49.0), and a subnormal divisor makes the reciprocal infinite. That path is polars-double-scalar-divisor.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

evidence.note: `test_list_arithmetic_values`, `Float32`: 1 // 0 is inf, 1 % 0 NaN, 1 / 0 inf, 0 // 0 NaN, 0 % 0 NaN, 0 / 0 NaN

notes: Pins the `Float32` floor remainder (-5 % 3 is 1, the divisor's sign) and NaN for a zero divisor (`1 % 0`, `0 % 0`).
